usage: python -m cleanroom.originality D:/n64work/drmario64/gate <clean assets dir> games/drmario64/spec --manifest games/drmario64/originality.json --report ORIGINALITY.md  (dirty root = the gate exports written by extract_more; clean root = the asset tree from games.drmario64.assets plus gate_inputs after build_decomp)

notes.music: 24 libmus songs composed by cleanroom.audio.compose from tempo, intro/loop lengths, channel roles/registers and our mood tags; retail notes only exported as MIDI on the dirty side for this comparison. Sound effects regenerated (same instrument setup, length and note count; new pitches/rhythm).
notes.text: Every US string (msg files, C string tables, debug menu, credits) rewritten by us; names.json maps every retail proper noun and staff name.
notes.geometry: Only real 3D meshes are compared (10). 309 rectangle cards and 119 flat cut-outs (now rectangles) are generic layout primitives rebuilt from rounded boxes and are exempt.
notes.images: All 1205 textures are new designs; retail PNGs are read only for this comparison.
notes.code: clean_text.bin = .text of the boot and main segments of our GCC build with the four RSP microcode blobs blanked (retail microcode is carried unchanged: publishing blocker). Allowed ('compiled'): the link-order .text runs of the objects our build compiled or assembled from decomp sources (gate_code/compiled), so the check proves the code region holds nothing but compiler/assembler output; short accessor functions that GCC and KMC happen to encode identically are explained this way. The retail side is all retail executable code (boot + main_segment text).
notes.ipl3: Our own CC0 boot stub (games/drmario64/ipl3/ipl3.s): boots in emulators, not on real consoles.
